scientific_question: Is the association between commuting burden and sleep time more negative than that with leisure time?
falsifiable_claim: sleep_weekday_min coefficient is more negative than leisure_weekday_min coefficient

observed_evidence.statement: Adjusted sleep_weekday_min coefficient = -48.711 (95% pointwise CI [-63.481, -33.94]; Bonferroni outcome interval [-67.565, -29.856])
Adjusted leisure_weekday_min coefficient = -20.396 (95% pointwise CI [-43.436, 2.644]; Bonferroni outcome interval [-49.808, 9.015])
Paired comparisons sleep vs leisure difference = -28.314 (interval [-66.17, 9.541])

scientific_inference.statement: Sleep time shows a stronger negative point estimate than leisure time.
The paired comparison interval includes zero, so the difference is not statistically distinguished.

unresolved_uncertainty: It remains uncertain whether the true difference between sleep and leisure associations is negative.

supporting_observation: The sleep coefficient is more negative than the leisure coefficient.
contradicting_observation: The sleep coefficient is not more negative than the leisure coefficient.

engine_capability_assessment.reason: Engine can estimate coefficients for both outcomes and compute their difference via paired comparison.
engine_capability_assessment.assessed_by: hypothesis_agent (provisional; the Experiment Planner decides feasibility)

limitations: Inference relies on linear specification and approximated variance.
Bonferroni adjustment limits power for detecting difference.

source_artifacts.integrity: content identical; LF checkout of CRLF-validated bytes

provenance.validation: contract, approved variables, observational language, numbers traceable to sources
